newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somalia Islamic Al-Ittihad leader wounded.
newsitem.headline: Somalia Islamic Al-Ittihad leader wounded.

text.p: The commander of the armed wing of Somalia's Islamic fundamentalist Al-Ittihad Al-Islam (Islamic Unity) militia has been wounded in an ambush, Al-Ittihad officials said.

Colonel Hassan Dahir Aweys was admitted to hospital in the capital on Thursday after the ambush on Wednesday night close to Bale-Dogle airport, 90 km (56 miles) west of Mogadishu. Another Al-Ittihad officer, Mohamed Kedie Afrah ,was killed.

The two were taking reinforcements in three vehicles from the capital towards southern Gedo region where they are fighting Marehan clansmen of the Somali National Front (SNF). No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.
Aid and security sources in Nairobi said earlier this month Ethiopian troops and SNF allies were in full control of an area inside Somalia after driving Al-Ittihad out of a stronghold.
Al-Ittihad withdrew from the area but was preparing to counter-attack once Ethiopian forces left, the aid officials said on Thursday.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Meles Zenawi denied last Saturday his forces were involved in the fighting and vowed to hunt down and hit Al-Ittihad unless it stopped attacks on Ethiopia.
Ethiopia blames Al-Ittihad for a series of attacks on soft targets in Ethiopia.
Al-Ittihad officials said the ambush, the first in territory controlled by faction leader Hussein Aideed, was aimed at undermining attacks they planned against SNF and Ethiopian forces.

Al-Ittihad set up its headquarters in Somalia's Luq in 1992, a year after central government collapsed in the Horn of Africa country. Since 1991 Somalia has drifted through civil war and anarchy although most of the country is now relatively peaceful. There is no unified army to protect frontiers.

In another development, aid agencies in Mogadishu and the port town of Merca suspended operations for a day to mourn the killing of a Portuguese doctor with the aid agency Doctors Without Borders (MSF) on June 21.
